title: Blue vs. green
summary: Switch a field between discrete and continuous on Columns or Color, and a date between parts and values, and watch headers turn into an axis.
intro: Pick a field and a shelf, then switch the pill between discrete (blue) and continuous (green). The view keeps `SUM(Minutes Watched)` as the other half of the chart, so only the pill you change differs. Watch what each colour draws, and which fields refuse to turn green.

copy.discrete: Blue on Rows or Columns draws headers: one label per member, in separate panes with nothing in between two members.
copy.continuous: Green on Rows or Columns draws an axis: a range from a minimum to a maximum with tick marks, where any value in between has a place.
copy.discreteColor: Blue on Color gives a categorical palette: a distinct colour per member and a legend that lists them.
copy.continuousColor: Green on Color gives a quantitative legend: a gradient, a continuous range of colours instead of one colour per member.
copy.stringOnly: Dimensions with a data type of String or Boolean can't be continuous: there's no number line for "Drama". Date and numeric dimensions, and all measures, can be either.
copy.datePart: A date part is discrete. It is one part of the date, aggregated across everything else: as a part, MONTH or QUARTER merges the years, so each header adds up the same month or quarter of every year. Good for seasonality.
copy.dateValue: A date value (a truncated date, from the lower, continuous section of the date menu) keeps the year, so the periods run along a timeline in order. Good for a trend.
copy.measureDiscrete: A measure made discrete is still a measure, so it is still aggregated. It just draws headers instead of an axis.
copy.role: Switching between blue and green never changes whether a field is a dimension or a measure.
